description: Cardinal direction (north/south/east/west) spatial reformulations for visual FCI items, adapted from West (2023).
source: Adapted from C.G. West, 'Advances in apparent conceptual physics reasoning in GPT-4', arXiv:2303.17012

items.text:
A ball rolls smoothly through a curved track that forms a half-circle on top of a flat table. At the moment the ball is halfway through the track, it is moving due north. Consider the possible forces acting on it at that instant:

A) A force pulling straight downward.
B) A force pushing straight east.
C) A force pushing straight north.
D) A force pushing straight west.

Which set of forces is acting on the ball?
1. Force A only
2. Forces A and B
3. Forces A and C
4. Forces A, B, and C
5. Forces A, C, and D

items.text:
A ball rolls through a curved track shaped like part of a circle and then exits onto a perfectly smooth, frictionless tabletop. At the instant it leaves the track, the ball is moving due east. Which path will the ball most closely follow after leaving the track?

1. A path that curves gradually toward the north.
2. A path that continues straight east.
3. A path that curves gradually toward the south.
4. A path that curves gradually toward the west.
5. A path that immediately heads straight north.

items.text:
A steel ball is attached to a string and is swung in a circular path in a horizontal plane. Consider a moment in the ball's motion when the ball is moving due north. At that moment, the string breaks near the ball. Which of the following paths would the ball most closely follow after the string breaks?

(a) It will initially travel north, but will quickly begin to curve to the west.
(b) It will travel north in a straight line.
(c) It will travel northeast in a straight line.
(d) It will initially travel east, but will quickly begin to curve north.
(e) It will travel east in a straight line.

items.text:
A hockey puck is sliding with constant speed v_0 toward the east on a frictionless horizontal surface. Forces from the air are negligible. When the puck reaches a certain point, it receives a swift horizontal kick toward the north. If the puck had been at rest when it received this kick, it would have started moving north with a speed v_k.

Which path will the puck most closely follow after receiving the kick?

1. It will travel straight north.
2. It will travel in a straight line toward the northeast.
3. It will continue straight east, after a shift northward.
4. It will curve gradually toward the north.
5. It will start moving north, then curve gradually toward the east.

items.text:
A ball is launched horizontally from the top of a cliff, from a cannon pointing due east. The flat ground below extends east from the cliff base. Air resistance is negligible. The ball lands on the ground some distance east of the base.

Which path will the ball most closely follow?

1. A straight diagonal line from the launch point to the landing point.
2. A smooth curve downward from the launch point to the landing point.
3. Straight east for a short distance, then curving downward to the landing point.
4. Straight east for some distance, then curved, then vertical some time before landing.
5. Straight east until nearly above the landing point, then vertical to the ground.

items.text:
A bowling ball falls from the cargo bay of an airplane flying due east in a straight, level path. Air resistance is negligible. An observer on the ground, watching from the south, watches the ball after it leaves the airplane.

Which path will the ball most closely follow?

1. A curve going toward the west and toward the ground.
2. Straight down toward the ground.
3. A straight line aimed down toward the east.
4. A curve going east and toward the ground.
5. Straight east for a while, then straight toward the ground.

items.text:
A child swings on a rope tied to a branch (point O). His movement starts above a point A and then continues downward through the point A. Consider the following distinct forces:
1. A downward force of gravity.
2. A force exerted by the rope pointing from A to O.
3. A force in the direction of the boy's motion.
4. A force pointing from O to A.
Which of the above forces is (are) acting on the boy when he is at position A?
(A) 1 only.
(B) 1 and 2.
(C) 1 and 3.
(D) 1, 2, and 3.
(E) 1, 3, and 4.

items.text:
Two blocks move along the same straight track in the same direction. Positions are measured every 0.2 s in length units (LU). Times t_1, t_2, t_3, ... indicate the same moments for both blocks.

Block A: t_1: 2 LU, t_2: 4 LU, t_3: 7 LU, t_4: 11 LU, t_5: 16 LU, t_6: 22 LU, t_7: 29 LU
Block B: t_1: 0 LU, t_2: 4 LU, t_3: 8 LU, t_4: 12 LU, t_5: 16 LU, t_6: 20 LU, t_7: 24 LU, t_8: 28 LU

Do the blocks ever have the same speed?

1. No.
2. Yes, at instant t_2.
3. Yes, at instant t_5.
4. Yes, at instants t_2 and t_5.
5. Yes, at some time during the interval t_3 to t_4.

Two blocks move along the same straight track toward the east. Positions are measured every 0.2 s in length units (LU). Identical time labels indicate the same moments for both blocks.

Block A: t_1: 2 LU, t_2: 6 LU, t_3: 10 LU, t_4: 14 LU, t_5: 18 LU, t_6: 22 LU, t_7: 26 LU
Block B: t_1: 0 LU, t_2: 6 LU, t_3: 12 LU, t_4: 18 LU, t_5: 24 LU

How are the accelerations of the blocks related?

A. The acceleration of A is greater than the acceleration of B.
B. The acceleration of A equals the acceleration of B. Both accelerations are greater than zero.
C. The acceleration of B is greater than the acceleration of A.
D. The acceleration of A equals the acceleration of B. Both accelerations are zero.
E. Not enough information is given to answer the question.

items.text:
A rocket drifts in outer space from point A to point B, moving toward the east. Starting at position B, the rocket's engine is turned on and produces a constant thrust toward the north. This thrust is maintained until the rocket reaches a point C.

Which path below best represents the path of the rocket between points B and C?

1. Point C lies northeast of point B. The path from B to C starts toward north, and curves smoothly toward northeast.
2. Point C lies directly north of point B. The path from B to C is straight toward north.
3. Point C lies northeast of point B. The path from B to C is straight.
4. Point C lies northeast of point B. The path from B to C continues toward east for a bit, then curves toward north, then continues straight toward northeast.
5. Point C lies northeast of point B. The path from B to C starts toward east, and curves smoothly toward northeast.

A rocket drifts in outer space from point A to point B, moving toward the east. Starting at position B, the rocket's engine is turned on and produces a constant thrust toward the north. This thrust is maintained until the rocket reaches a point C. At point C, the rocket's engine is turned off and the thrust immediately drops to zero.

Which path will the rocket follow beyond point C?

1. The path goes straight toward the east.
2. The path goes straight toward the northeast.
3. The path goes straight toward the north.
4. The path goes toward the east and curves smoothly upward.
5. The path goes toward the east and curves smoothly downward.
